title: Multi-word positional arguments to MCP prompts don't seem to work
body:
### What happened?

I called an MCP prompt with a single argument:

```
/my_command these are some words
```

My MCP server received just `"these"` as an argument.

So I tried escaping:

```
/my_command "these are some words"
```

My MCP server received just `'"these'` as an argument.

### What did you expect to happen?

I would expect:

1. If a prompt only has a single argument, the entire string after `/command_name` is passed as that argument.
2. If a prompt has multiple arguments, then splat all remaining spaced words into the last argument.
3. If a user escapes with quotes, respect the quotes and treat as a single argument.

linked_prs.title: feat(mcp): Improve MCP prompt argument parsing
linked_prs.body:
## TLDR

Enhances the argument parser for MCP prompts to correctly handle multi-word, quoted, and escaped arguments.

The key changes include:
- Implementing a more robust parser to correctly parse arguments, respecting quotes and escape characters.
- Adding a comprehensive test suite to validate the new parsing logic and prevent future regressions.

## Dive Deeper

If there is only one positional argument to fill in, then all the arguments are considered a part of that one argument and we don't require the user to quote them. Otherwise, individual arguments must be wrapped in quotes.

This behavior was requested in the original issue but we could remove it if we want to reduce the complexity a bit here.

## Reviewer Test Plan

Just run the tests, or hook up an MCP server that supports prompts and try out mixes of argument styles.
